Class TrainingSpec

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.gradle.TrainingSpec
public abstract class TrainingSpec extends Object
How a training run exercises the application: how the build knows it is ready, what it asks of it and how it stops it. It is the training { } block of the MicronautRunnerExtension, and each task that launches the application takes its own copy, whose conventions are the block's values. 
micronaut {
    runner {
        training {
            readinessPath = '/health'
            workloadPaths = ['/hello', '/orders']
        }
    }
}

There is one property for each component of TrainingSettings, which documents them and owns their defaults and their validation. A path is the path of an HTTP request to the application on the loopback interface.

The API is experimental: it may change in any release.

Since:
1.0

    • getReadinessPath

      @Input @Optional public abstract org.gradle.api.provider.Property<String> getReadinessPath()
      The path to GET until it answers 2xx, once the port accepts a connection. Without it the accepted connection alone means ready.
      Returns:
      the readiness path

    • getWorkloadPaths

      @Input @Optional public abstract org.gradle.api.provider.ListProperty<String> getWorkloadPaths()
      The paths to GET in order, each of which must answer 2xx. When this and getWorkloadCommand() are both empty, the application serves one GET / and the build warns: the workload decides which classes a training run sees.
      Returns:
      the workload paths

    • getWorkloadRepeat

      @Input @Optional public abstract org.gradle.api.provider.Property<Integer> getWorkloadRepeat()
      How many times the whole list of getWorkloadPaths() is requested. Defaults to 1.
      Returns:
      the repeat count

    • getWorkloadCommand

      @Input @Optional public abstract org.gradle.api.provider.ListProperty<String> getWorkloadCommand()
      A command and its arguments, run after the paths with MICRONAUT_RUNNER_TRAINING_URL set to the application's base URL. It must exit with status 0 within getWorkloadTimeout().
      Returns:
      the workload command

    • getRunToExit

      @Input @Optional public abstract org.gradle.api.provider.Property<Boolean> getRunToExit()
      Whether the application ends by itself, as one that is not a server does. There is then no readiness check, no workload and no stop; the application must exit with status 0 within getReadinessTimeout(). Defaults to false.
      Returns:
      the run-to-exit flag

    • getStopPath

      @Input @Optional public abstract org.gradle.api.provider.Property<String> getStopPath()
      The path to POST to stop the application, where an orderly stop needs a request rather than a signal, as on Windows. Without it the process is destroyed.
      Returns:
      the stop path
